name: Karnak Temple Complex
category: Ancient Temple Complex / UNESCO World Heritage Site

location.region: Upper Egypt (ancient Thebes, East Bank of the Nile)

historical_description: Karnak is the largest religious building complex ever constructed, covering roughly 100 hectares. Known to the ancient Egyptians as Ipet-Isut ('the most select of places'), it was the principal cult center of the god Amun-Ra and, alongside Luxor Temple, formed the heart of religious life in ancient Thebes. Unlike most temples built by a single ruler, Karnak was continuously expanded, modified, and embellished by successive pharaohs over roughly 2,000 years, from the Middle Kingdom through the Ptolemaic period, making it a layered record of Egyptian architectural and religious history. The complex includes the Precinct of Amun-Re, the Precinct of Mut, the Precinct of Montu, and the dismantled Temple of Amenhotep IV (Akhenaten), along with the famed Great Hypostyle Hall.

construction_details.construction_period: circa 2000 BCE to around 100 CE (over roughly 2,000 years of continuous additions)
construction_details.main_contributors: Senusret I (Middle Kingdom founder), Thutmose I, Thutmose III, Hatshepsut, Amenhotep III, Seti I, Ramesses II, and later Ptolemaic rulers
construction_details.great_hypostyle_hall: 134 massive sandstone columns arranged in 16 rows, built primarily under Seti I and completed by Ramesses II, covering about 5,000 square meters; the largest central columns reach approximately 21 meters (69 feet) high
construction_details.materials: Primarily sandstone, with granite obelisks and elements
construction_details.notable_features: Avenue of ram-headed sphinxes, the sacred lake, multiple pylons (10 in total), obelisks of Hatshepsut and Thutmose I

dynasty: Primarily Middle Kingdom origins with major New Kingdom expansion (18th–20th Dynasties), continuing into the Ptolemaic period

opening_hours.sound_and_light_show: Evening shows typically run at staggered times (e.g., 19:00, 20:15, 21:30) with rotating language narration

ticket_price.notes: Prices are set by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities and subject to periodic revision; confirm current rates via egymonuments.com or at the ticket office.

best_visiting_time.time_of_day: Early morning at opening (cooler temperatures, smaller crowds) or late afternoon after large tour groups depart
best_visiting_time.season: October to April for milder weather
best_visiting_time.avoid: Midday hours (10:00–14:00), which combine peak heat and peak crowds
best_visiting_time.evening_option: The Sound and Light Show offers a dramatically lit nighttime experience of the temple

interesting_facts: Karnak is the second most-visited ancient monument in Egypt after the Pyramids of Giza.
The complex was expanded by more pharaohs than any other site in Egypt, with contributions spanning roughly two millennia.
The Great Hypostyle Hall's 134 columns are so massive that ancient builders reportedly required about 5 men to encircle the largest columns.
Karnak's sacred lake was used by priests for ritual purification and reflects the surrounding temple architecture.
An avenue of sphinxes once physically connected Karnak Temple to Luxor Temple, about 2.7 km away; sections of this avenue have been excavated and restored.
Karnak was dedicated primarily to the Theban triad: the god Amun-Ra, his consort Mut, and their son Khonsu.
unesco_status: Part of UNESCO World Heritage Site 'Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis' (inscribed 1979)
accessibility_notes: Mostly flat paved and packed-earth paths suitable for most visitors, though some areas have uneven ancient stone flooring; limited wheelchair accessibility in certain inner sanctuaries.
nearest_airport: Luxor International Airport (LXR), approx. 8 km away
